neighbours.label: keeping things as they are: continue / maintain / retain / preserve and the 'current', 'existing' or 'usual' thing that is kept; the + pole is the other side (replace, new, instead)
fire: Under the agreement the clinic will continue to see patients at its old address.
The council decided to maintain the existing speed limit on the coast road.
Shareholders voted in favour of retaining the present chairman for a third term.
The school intends to preserve its long-standing uniform policy.
Ferries will continue to sail from the north pier throughout the winter.
The treaty allows both countries to maintain their current fishing quotas.
Most villagers wanted to keep the traditional market day unchanged.
The new owners promised to retain all of the existing staff.
quiet: Under the agreement the clinic will stop seeing patients at its old address.
The council decided to lower the speed limit on the coast road.
Shareholders voted in favour of removing the chairman before his third term.
The school intends to scrap its uniform policy next autumn.
Ferries will no longer sail from the north pier during the winter.
The treaty forces both countries to halve their fishing quotas.
Most villagers wanted to move the market day to Saturday.
The new owners promised to hire forty additional staff.

notes: Card: peak ' continue' x10, ' maintain' x3, ' normal' x3, 'maintien du', ' retaining'; the + pole's top examples are 'replaces', 'supplant', 'a new', 'instead'. Probes: 'maintain the current fee structure' 0.70, 'retaining the old voting rules' 0.68, 'will continue to operate' 0.34, 'kept running on the usual timetable' 0.27; 'cease to operate' 0.05, 'replace the current fee structure' 0.03, 'abolishing the old voting rules' 0.01.
